[FAILURE-TRACE-2026]
Title: Captured package-test failure
Date: 2026-07-21

The command exits during Nx initialization with Failed to start plugin worker. There is no Jest banner, no test-file path, no assertion output, and no TypeScript diagnostic. The trace therefore proves the test runner did not start; it does not show that the package tests or product code failed.

[MAIN-CHECKOUT-PASS-2026]
Title: Comparison run in the main checkout
Date: 2026-07-21

The same focused test target completed in the main checkout with 14 tests passing. This comparison increases confidence that the worktree environment is the immediate problem, but it does not by itself prove that every worktree dependency and configuration matches the main checkout.

[WORKTREE-DEPS-2026]
Title: Dependency setup in worktrees
Date: 2026-06-29

A worktree that lacks node_modules should link to the main checkout node_modules before invoking repository scripts. NODE_PATH can help resolution, but the symlink matters because scripts call binaries under the worktree node_modules path. If the branch changes the lockfile or dependencies, the shared install may be stale and must be treated as an environment risk.

[NODE-POLICY-2026]
Title: Supported Node runtime for repository checks
Date: 2026-05-17

Use the repository-pinned Node 22 runtime for Nx, Jest, and TypeScript checks. Failures during plugin initialization under a newer unsupported Node version are environment evidence, not product-test evidence. Record the active version before changing code.

[NX-RUNBOOK-2026]
Title: Focused Nx recovery runbook
Date: 2026-07-08

For Failed to start plugin worker, first run npx nx reset and retry the exact focused command. Keep the test target and flags unchanged so the retry remains comparable. If sandbox restrictions still prevent worker startup, rerun the same focused command with the required approval outside that restriction. Do not widen to a repository-wide test as a substitute.

[REINSTALL-GUIDE-2023]
Title: Archived clean-install troubleshooting
Date: 2023-09-02

This archived generic guide suggests deleting node_modules and the lockfile before reinstalling every dependency. It predates Nx plugin workers and worktree dependency sharing. Repository maintainers no longer use it as the first response to plugin startup failures.

Title: Common Jest assertion failures
Date: 2026-04-04

Jest assertion failures include the failing test name, expected and received values, and a stack trace. None of those signals appears when Nx fails before starting its plugin worker.

item.text:
This proves Nx failed during startup, before Jest ran. It does not prove that any test, TypeScript code, or product behavior is broken, because there’s no Jest banner, failing test name, assertion output, or TypeScript diagnostic [FAILURE-TRACE-2026] [JEST-FAILURE-CATALOG-2026].

Use this smallest verification sequence:

1. **Check Node.** Record `node --version` and confirm the repository-pinned Node 22 runtime is active. Plugin initialization failures under unsupported Node versions are environment failures, not test results [NODE-POLICY-2026].

2. **Check worktree dependencies.** Confirm the worktree has `node_modules` linked to the main checkout. `NODE_PATH` alone isn’t enough because repository scripts use binaries under the worktree’s own `node_modules` path. Also check whether the branch changed the lockfile or dependencies, since that can make the shared install stale [WORKTREE-DEPS-2026].

3. **Reset Nx and retry unchanged.** Run `npx nx reset`, then rerun the exact package test command with the same target and flags. Changing or widening the test command would make the comparison less useful [NX-RUNBOOK-2026].

4. **Remove the execution restriction if needed.** If the same command still cannot start the worker because of sandbox restrictions, request approval and run that same focused command outside the sandbox. Don’t substitute a repository-wide test [NX-RUNBOOK-2026].

The matching target already passed 14 tests in the main checkout, which strongly points to the worktree environment as the immediate cause, though it doesn’t prove both checkouts have identical dependencies and configuration [MAIN-CHECKOUT-PASS-2026]. Don’t delete `node_modules`, remove the lockfile, reinstall everything, or change product code at this stage. That old reinstall advice predates the current worktree setup and is no longer the first response to this failure [REINSTALL-GUIDE-2023].
